lastText: File ClosedThe Road Not Taken to AthensContestedSoviet High Command, 1941 — 1945End of hostilities: JUNE 1945 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives close to the historical schedule, around June 1945. The human cost of this path lands close to the historical one — among the highest of any combatant nation in the war by a wide margin, roughly 27 million dead, military and civilian combined. The industrial evacuation was subordinated to front supply in 1941 — easing that autumn's crisis at a cost in Urals production capacity that every later year of this campaign quietly pays for. The push straight for Berlin in February was actually attempted here — testing Chuikov's postwar claim against the flank risk Zhukov's own staff warned about, rather than leaving the question a memoir argument. The autumn 1942 reserve was weighted entirely south — Mars never launched, the Rzhev grinder's cost declined, and the single-theater concentration tested against the pinning argument Mars's defenders always made. Germany's defeat was not a variable Soviet command decisions controlled, only its timing and its price.One Year LaterVictory arrived close to the historical May 8, 1945, and the year that follows tracks the historical one closely: the Red Army's occupation zone, the machinery of a new political order installed behind it, and a wartime alliance already audibly disagreeing about what Europe's map is supposed to mean now that the shooting has stopped.
